subject: Proposal: Availability Annex & Order Form Language for QuantumMed MSA
messages:
From: Sujata Rao <sujata@quantummed.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@quantummed.com
Date: 2027-05-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: availability annex & order form language for MSA

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — QuantumMed’s infra and security teams reviewed Redwood’s runtime details and we want to move toward an enterprise MSA. Procurement asked me to surface two items up front before we send a PO: a concise annex for availability (uptime/latency commitments) and a brief, redline-friendly order form snippet we can plug into our MSA/SOW appendix.

High-level asks:
- A clear SLA annex that covers (a) service availability % by deployment type (hosted API / dedicated pools / private), (b) latency SLOs for synchronous endpoints (p50/p95) on the hosted tier, and (c) remedies/credits for breaches.
- Explicit exception language for scheduled maintenance windows and DDoS/force majeure events.
- We would like an outline we can give to legal for a targeted review — procurement prefers a one-page order form clause plus an annex doc with definitions and measurement methods.

Attached: QuantumMed_MSA_Draft.pdf and an infrastructure matrix so you can map which systems will be on Hosted vs. Dedicated.

Can you propose language and a target timeline? We’re aiming to finalize order form language by end of next week (5/28) to hit our quarter procurement cadence.

Thanks,
Sujata Rao
Head of Procurement, QuantumMed
[Attachment: QuantumMed_MSA_Draft.pdf]
[Attachment: Attachment A - Infrastructure Matrix.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sujata Rao <sujata@quantummed.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability annex & order form language for MSA

Hi Sujata — appreciate the clear ask and the matrix. Looping in Marissa (your AE) and Karthik (security/compliance) so we can scope and get legal involved early.

Quick notes / proposed approach:
- We can draft a short "Availability Annex" that separates commitments by deployment mode. Typical starting points we use internally: Hosted API: 99.9% availability; Dedicated pools (reserved GPU capacity): 99.95%; Private (on-prem/VPC): availability is customer-dependent, we provide best-effort instrumentation + optional availability commitment with an Ops addendum.
- For latency SLOs: we propose publishing p50/p95 targets per endpoint in the annex, with an explicit measurement method (rolling 30-day window, regional measurement).
- Remedies: standard service credits tied to monthly uptime percentage with escalating bands. We can include optional SLA buyups (higher credits for elevated SLA) if QuantumMed needs tougher guarantees for a subset of endpoints.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance, emergency security patches, and third-party network outages will be called out with an escrow/notification protocol.

I attached an initial scratch draft of an annex and a short order form snippet for your legal to review. Can your procurement team confirm whether they want credits capped at $X or a % of monthly fees? That affects the redline significantly.

Next steps I propose:
1) QuantumMed confirms whether they want 99.95 vs 99.9 for Hosted for mission-critical endpoints.
2) We send a redline-ready annex + order form by EOD 5/23; Karthik will include evidence for our measurement (metrics, monitoring links).
3) If accepted, we’ll produce a DocuSign-ready attachment for signature.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Annex_v0.3.docx]
[Attachment: OrderForm_SLA_Language.txt]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sujata Rao <sujata@quantummed.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-23T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability annex & order form language for MSA

Hi Sujata — following up with a more concrete proposal so procurement has something to circulate to legal. Below is the short order-form clause + an annex outline. I kept it concise for redlining.

Order form snippet (editable):
"Service Commitment: Redwood Inference will provide the Services described in the Order Form in accordance with the Availability Annex attached hereto as Exhibit A. The Availability Annex sets forth the measurement methodology, availability targets, and remedies for failure to meet those targets."

Annex highlights (to include in Exhibit A):
- Definitions: "Available", "Downtime", "Impaired", "Excluded Events"
- Measurement: regional measurement points, 30-day rolling window, token-weighted URL set for API endpoints
- Availability targets (proposed): Hosted API default: 99.90% (can be elevated to 99.95% for named endpoints via Order Form); Dedicated: 99.95%; Private deployments: defined in Ops Addendum
- Latency targets (proposed): sync endpoints p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for Hosted (measured at edge POPs); Dedicated targets to be provided post-capacity mapping
- Remedies: Service Credits by monthly uptime percentage with the first band starting at <99.90% = 10% credit; second band <99.50% = 30% credit; material breaches subject to negotiation
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours notice for non-emergency), DDoS mitigations, force majeure

Procurement questions we need answered to finalize redlines:
- Are credits capped at a dollar amount or left as %?
- Do you want a fixed SLA for a named list of endpoints or per-deployment type?
- Any internal compliance evidence QuantumMed needs (SOC2 report, audit logs)?

If you confirm the credit cap preference and whether there are named endpoints requiring 99.95, we’ll circulate RFC redlines by EOD 5/24 and include a short evidence packet.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sujata Rao <sujata@quantummed.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-24T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability annex & order form language for MSA — redlines and evidence pack

Hi all — attaching redlines on the annex and an evidence summary for QuantumMed’s compliance team. Key technical clarifications included in the redlines:

- Measurement window: clarified to be "rolling 30-day window with hourly sampling" and a publicized test suite of endpoints we measure against (we included a small token-weighted list in Exhibit B).
- Defined the process for "named endpoints" elevation: Order Form must enumerate the endpoints and specify billing/commitment change.
- Clarified Scheduled Maintenance: We propose a default 6-hour weekly maintenance window with 72-hour advance notice for planned events >30 minutes; emergency patches invoked by security events are excluded but Redwood will provide post-incident reports.
- Remedies: replaced uncapped dollar-language with percentage-of-monthly-fees; propose a cap equal to 200% of the monthly recurring fees for the affected service line (this keeps commercial risk bounded).

Attachments included: Redwood_Annex_QM_v1_redlines.docx (redlined annex), Availability_Evidence_Summary.pdf (SOC2 attestation pointer + sample uptime graphs), and a short order-form text file for procurement.

Sujata — if procurement is comfortable with the %-based credits and the proposed cap, we can prepare a DocuSign packet by EOD 5/25. If you prefer a fixed dollar cap, please indicate the amount so we can adjust the redlines.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
[Attachment: Redwood_Annex_QM_v1_redlines.docx]
[Attachment: Availability_Evidence_Summary.pdf]
